3.6.1.officialText: locate approximately a root of an equation, by means of graphical considerations and/or searching for a sign change
3.6.1.spineTitleVerbatim: locate approximately a root of an equation, by means of graphical considerations and/or searching for a sign change

resources.title: When does this exponential function equal this linear one?
resources.evidence: The well demands the graph then 'Use your graph to find the roots of the equation 3^x=3x+2'; the solution reads both intersections off the plot to two decimal places (x=-0.48 and x=1.83, checked against the exact -0.4673.../1.8344...) - locating roots by graphical considerations, 3.6.1 verbatim. Supersedes its stale lane-3-logarithmic-and-exponential-functions non-overlap row of record.

resources.title: How many real roots does this cubic polynomial have?
resources.evidence: The purest sign-change search in the corpus: the solution tabulates f(x) across x=-2..6, reads three sign changes bracketing three real roots ('one between x=-2 and x=-1; one between 1 and 2; a third between 5 and 6'), then hones the negative root between -1.3 and -1.2 (f(-1.25)=0.671875>0) to conclude x=-1.3 to one decimal place - locating a root by searching for a sign change and refining the bracket, the verbatim 3.6.1 skill.

resources.title: Can we calculate an approximation to the root of this function?
resources.evidence: The well derives the chord-intercept approximation (af(b) - bf(a))/(f(b) - f(a)) from the sign-bracketed interval f(a) < 0 < f(b) and applies it to x^2 + x^(1/2) - 37 = 0 ('find two consecutive integers between which a root lies... calculate an approximation to the root, giving three significant figures') - locating a root by a graphical/linear-interpolation consideration between two sign-change bounds (the method r8679's survey names 'linear interpolation'), riding the standing 1.3.1/1.3.2 alignments of record.

resources.title: Can we show this quartic equation has exactly two real roots?
resources.evidence: 'Find the positive root of the equation correct to one decimal place': the solution reads ~1.4 off the sketch (graphical consideration), tabulates f(1.3)/f(1.4)/f(1.5), and applies the continuity + sign-change law ('As there is a sign change and the function is continuous, the root we seek must fall between 1.3 and 1.4'), refined by trial and improvement to 1.4 - riding the standing 1.3.2 alignment of record.

resources.title: A cubic has one real root—can we find an approximation to it?
resources.evidence: Method 1 is trial-and-improvement interval refinement to three decimal places; Method 3 is the Newton-Raphson iteration in x_{n+1} notation ('x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n)', here x_{n+1} = x_n - (x^3+3x^2-3)/(3x^2+6x)); and the uniqueness argument ('since the curve is continuous... it must cut the x-axis somewhere between x=0 and x=1') is sign-change reasoning - 3.6.1 and 3.6.3 ride beside the standing 1.7.3 alignment of record.

resources.title: Can we find the repeated root for  $4x^4+x^2+3x+1=0$?
resources.evidence: Locating the repeated root via f': 'f'(x) must have a root between -1 and 0, since f'(x) is continuous and we have a change of sign. The value -1/2 is a sensible choice to test' - sign-change root location used as the instrument bounding the double root, beside the standing 1.7.2/3.1.4 alignments of record (medium: instrumental step, not the target skill).

resources.title: See the power
resources.evidence: The solution bounds x between 1.25 and 1.5 and narrows the bracket ('We could narrow this range by trial and improvement or by plotting a graph') before the exact digit-counting logarithms take over - interval-search root location beside the standing 3.2.1 alignment (medium: instrumental, subordinate to the log-law purpose).

resources.title: To log or not to log?
resources.evidence: The solution confronts 5^x = x^5 ('This is another example of an equation we don't know how to solve exactly. A sketch... might help') - the locate-approximately stance of 3.6.1 inside the standing 3.2.3 alignment (medium: the numerical method is advised, not executed to an answer).

3.6.2.officialText: understand the idea of, and use the notation for, a sequence of approximations which converges to a root of an equation
3.6.2.spineTitleVerbatim: understand the idea of, and use the notation for, a sequence of approximations which converges to a root of an equation

resources.title: If $x_1 = (x_0 + 2)/(x_0 + 1)$, can we show $\sqrt{2}$ lies between $x_0$ and $x_1$?
resources.evidence: The solution names the machinery verbatim ('Thus we have in action here the x = g(x) iteration, or the rearrangement method, where we start with f(x) = 0, and move to x = g(x)'), proves the alternating bracketing of sqrt(2) by consecutive terms, establishes the error decay |x_{n+1}^2 - 2| = |x_n^2 - 2|/(x_n+1)^2 < |x_n^2 - 2|, and drives the iteration to prescribed accuracy (41/29 and 99/70 differing from sqrt(2) by less than 5x10^-4) - the 3.6.2 sequence-of-approximations notation and the 3.6.3 iteration-based-on-a-rearrangement to a prescribed degree of accuracy. FLIP: rides its lane-6 whole-station body under UGM-Resources/pure-1-series (spec_points [] — unmapped-by-design under rule 3); supersedes its stale lane-1-series non-overlap row of record (the circular-slice precedent).

resources.title: Staircase sequences
resources.evidence: The solution sets up the self-similar fixed point ('If I call that x... x seems to reappear inside itself: x = 1 + 1/x'), rearranges to x^2 - x - 1 = 0 and identifies the limit as its positive root (1+sqrt(5))/2, with the term table (1, 2, 1.5, 1.666..., 1.6, 1.625, ...) a convergent sequence of approximations observed to alternate either side of the root - the 3.6.2 idea and the 3.6.3 relation between x = F(x) and the equation being solved, in an exploratory register.

resources.title: What is the area under the curve $y = \cos x - \sin x +2$?
resources.evidence: The solution surveys the numerical canon verbatim ('decimal search, binary search, linear interpolation, the rearrangement method or simply zooming in with graphing software') and executes Newton-Raphson from the given first approximation 1.5 to the second approximation 1.43 (3 sf) with a substitution check - the first/second-approximation language of 3.6.2 and a given-iteration application to prescribed accuracy under 3.6.3, riding the fresh lane-13 3.5.1 pick body.
